title: Evolution
standard_text: Evolution occurs at the population level: evidence for evolution, natural selection, mechanisms of evolutionary change (mutation, genetic drift, gene flow), artificial selection, and speciation (microevolution and macroevolution). (summary of BC's Curriculum, Life Sciences 11)
meta_desc: Free Life Sciences 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): evidence, natural selection and speciation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Mutation, selection, drift and gene flow change populations.
body_html:
How to think about it

Evidence for evolution comes from fossils, homologous structures, vestigial structures, embryos and DNA. Natural selection: individuals vary, some variations help survival and reproduction, and those traits become more common over generations.

Other mechanisms are mutation, genetic drift (chance changes, strongest in small populations) and gene flow (migration). Microevolution is small change within a population; macroevolution is the formation of new species and larger groups. Speciation happens when populations are isolated and can no longer interbreed.

Example

A bat wing and a human arm have the same bones. What kind of structures are these?

Same origin, different use

Answer: homologous

Example

A small population loses an allele by chance. What is this?

Not selection

Answer: genetic drift

Common mistakes

  • Thinking individuals evolve.
  • Mixing up homologous and analogous structures.
  • Thinking natural selection makes the traits an organism needs.

faq.q: Why are antibiotic-resistant bacteria an example of evolution?
faq.a: The population changes as resistant bacteria survive and reproduce.
When two groups can no longer interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
